content: A pulmonary mass is defined as any area of pulmonary opacification within the lung that measures more than 30 mm in diameter. Pulmonary masses can be either benign or malignant in nature. In contrast, a pulmonary nodule is characterized as a relatively well-defined, round or oval lesion located in the pulmonary parenchyma, with a diameter equal to or smaller than 30 mm. Pulmonary nodules can be further categorized into two types: solitary nodules or multiple nodules. For more detailed information about each specific type of condition, you can refer to the links provided in blue within the algorithm below.
